correctness.rationale: Every part has a common external-one count; homogeneous parts cannot become mixed. Mixed parts of a period-two state must tie in both phases, forcing an even number of reversing homogeneous parts. Two or more mixed parts must be balanced (n even), whereas exactly one mixed part permits any nonconstant assignment (r odd). Separately enumerating all-homogeneous states gives the claimed disjoint census. Exact occupancy and independent bit-level computations check 19 and 11 size pairs; 124400 direct labelled states checked. The proof covers all r>=4,n>=1.

originality.rationale: No inspected primary or accessible published finding establishes the all-r>=4 binary majority fixed/primitive-two census. The tripartite case does not imply the arbitrarily-many-balanced-mixed-part mechanism or its leading-power asymptotic; published multipartite parity automata use XOR, and majority C-colorings concern static graph colorings. The historical 1980 full text remains inaccessible and absolute priority is not certified.

value.rationale: A natural r-part blow-up graph family has a complete all-r initially recurrent census with new multi-mixed-part frozen mechanisms, an exact even/odd size and part-count transition, and a sharp leading oscillation growth law. For r>=4 this is not the three-part specialization: arbitrarily many frozen balanced parts coexist with two reversing uniform parts. The result provides structural invariant and entropy-scale information, not a re-tabulation of small cases.
